exposure: planned vaginal birth for breech presentation
planned cesarean section for breech presentation
outcome: ventilation support at < 6 h of life
ventilation support at > 6 h of life
cohort: The study included 546,842 term singleton breech deliveries of live babies without congenital anomalies in the United States between 2008 and 2017, divided into groups of planned vaginal birth and planned cesarean section.
finding: Planned vaginal birth for breech presentation was associated with an increased risk of adverse neonatal outcomes, including infant death, NICU admission, ventilation support, and low Apgar scores, compared to planned cesarean section.
mod_finding: Planned vaginal birth for breech presentation had a low success rate and was associated with increased risks of neonatal morbidity and mortality compared to planned cesarean section.
followup_time: Up to infant death (within the first year of life), with early neonatal outcomes measured at 5 minutes, <6 hours, and >6 hours of life.
